table.title: Mathematical Notation Reference
table.html:
SymbolNameLaTeXMeaning
∑Summation\sumDenotes the sum of a sequence of terms; an index and lower and upper bounds are usually written below and above the sign, as in ∑i=1n ai.
∫Integral\intRepresents an integral, used for antiderivatives and for definite integrals that accumulate a quantity over an interval or region; limits of integration may be attached to the sign.
∇Nabla\nablaA vector differential operator that produces the gradient of a scalar field and, depending on how it is combined with a vector field, the divergence or curl.
⊗Tensor product\otimesDenotes the tensor product of vector spaces or modules, or the Kronecker product of matrices; the intended construction is usually indicated by the surrounding context.
ℵ₀Aleph-null\aleph_0The cardinality of countably infinite sets such as the natural numbers; it is the smallest infinite cardinal number in standard set theory.
table.brief: Math notation table: Symbol (∑, ∫, ∇, ⊗, ℵ₀) / Name / LaTeX (like \otimes) / Meaning (long)

understanding.purpose: Provide a reference linking mathematical symbols to their names, LaTeX commands, and meanings.
understanding.reading: Readers can scan the symbol column to locate an entry, then read across for its name, command, and explanation; they may also compare names or commands down their columns.
groups: Symbol, Name, and LaTeX identify the same notation in three forms.
Meaning explains each notation and contains the longest prose.
keep_intact: Individual words in names and meanings
may_wrap: Meaning descriptions can wrap naturally at word boundaries.
Multiword names can wrap; their extra line may fit within the height already required by the meaning.

preferred.name: r0B
preferred.note: Use compact identifier columns and allow multiword names to wrap to give meanings the most room.

acceptable.name: r0A
acceptable.note: Keep names on one line and give the remaining space to the explanatory prose.

bad.name: r0C
bad.note: Give the three notation columns more breathing room for scanning while accepting more wrapping in meanings and longer names.
bad.why: The Symbol and LaTeX columns have surplus width while Meaning is crowded into a narrow measure. This produces long, tall rows and leaves large empty areas beside the descriptions.

rationale: r0B gives the descriptive Meaning column the most room while keeping every symbol and LaTeX command intact. Tensor product wraps in the Name column, but remains easy to identify within its row. r0A keeps that name on one line, though its narrower descriptions make the table noticeably taller.

general: Give long prose enough width to read comfortably, while reserving enough space to keep identifiers and headers intact.
Judge wrapping by its effect on scanning and row relationships, rather than treating every wrapped cell as a fault.
specific: The Symbol and LaTeX columns need little width beyond their longest entries.
Allowing Tensor product to wrap gives Meaning more room across all five entries.

tradeoffs: r0A favors an uninterrupted list of names; r0B favors shorter descriptions and a more compact table.
uncertain: The ranges are approximate and assume that the remaining width is redistributed proportionally while the total stays within 583px. Small width changes can alter individual line breaks, so equal quality would need confirmation in a browser.

critique.good: All headers, names, symbols, and commands stay on one line. The identifying columns are easy to scan.
critique.problems: The meanings form narrow blocks, making the rows tall and leaving substantial empty space beside the shorter identifiers.
critique.cause: The 137px Name column reserves enough space for Tensor product on one line, leaving only 277px for Meaning.

critique.good: The wider Meaning column improves prose flow and reduces row heights. Tensor product wraps cleanly, while headers, individual words, symbols, and commands remain intact. Rows still read clearly across the table.
critique.problems: The Integral explanation ends with a short final line, and the wrapped name takes two lines.
critique.cause: Meaning has 306px, which is insufficient to avoid every short line. Name has 108px, so Tensor product wraps at its word boundary.

critique.good: Headers, symbols, commands, and individual words remain intact, and the identifying columns are spacious.
critique.problems: The meanings are compressed into tall, narrow blocks, creating the longest rows and large areas of empty space in the identifying columns. Tensor product still wraps.
critique.cause: The 105px Symbol and LaTeX columns and 126px Name column leave only 247px for Meaning; the extra Name width is still insufficient to keep Tensor product on one line.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r0B.why: The compact identifier columns leave a generous measure for meanings, while symbols and LaTeX remain intact. The two-line Tensor product name is easy to read.

r0A.why: Every name stays on one line and the columns scan clearly, though the narrower Meaning column creates more wrapping and taller rows.

r0C.why: The identifiers are legible, but the wide Symbol and LaTeX columns leave less space for meanings; descriptions wrap heavily and Tensor product still occupies two lines.

ref_auto.why: The compact identifier columns give the descriptions a comfortable measure, with intact symbols and LaTeX. Tensor product wraps cleanly across two lines.

ref_equal.why: The nearly equal columns give short identifiers excessive space and squeeze meanings into very narrow, heavily wrapped passages. Tall rows make the entries harder to scan.

raw.unsure: A and D are visually almost identical; their small width differences do not produce a meaningful advantage in the rendered table.

ref_auto.why: The meaning column has comfortable line lengths, while symbols and LaTeX commands remain intact. Tensor product wraps, and the integral entry ends with a short isolated line.

r0B.why: The compact identifier columns leave ample room for meanings. Tensor product wraps, and the integral entry ends with an isolated word; the result is very close to A.

r0C.why: All identifiers remain readable, but the wider symbol and LaTeX columns leave a narrow meaning column, producing more wrapping and conspicuous empty space.

ref_equal.why: Equal column widths give excessive space to short symbols and commands while squeezing meanings into very short lines. Rows become exceptionally tall, and the formula is split across lines.

r0A.why: All names and LaTeX commands fit on one line, and the meaning column remains wide enough for readable prose. The columns reflect their content and the rows scan clearly.

raw.unsure: A and B give meanings more room and are nearly indistinguishable from each other; choosing E depends on the value placed on keeping every name on one line.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
